scenarios.name: atomic-transfer-with-rollback
scenarios.rationale: B meets every rubric item: db.transaction with an async callback, trx on every query, forUpdate() on the balance read, an Error thrown on insufficient funds, and decrement/increment for the updates. A uses a transaction, trx, forUpdate and throws, but it does the balance updates with raw SQL instead of decrement/increment, and it doesn't read the balance to check it before debiting.

scenarios.name: ts-migration-create-and-run
scenarios.rationale: A covers every rubric item: it runs npx knex init -x ts, uses migrate:make -x ts, sets extension 'ts', and uses enu with defaultTo, timestamps(true, true), references().inTable().onDelete('CASCADE'), and a down that drops posts first. It also runs migrate:latest with NODE_OPTIONS="--import tsx". B skips npx knex init -x ts, writes the knexfile by hand, and defaults to ts-node, so the tsx loader appears only as a side note. B's schema is otherwise correct, and its native enum and DROP TYPE handling is a useful extra.

scenarios.name: monthly-orders-report-postgres
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric's query form closely (db.raw DATE_TRUNC, sum('amount as total'), count('* as orders'), groupByRaw, orderBy month desc) and explains the string cause with both cast-in-SQL and in-code fixes, while B uses raw SUM/COUNT casts instead of sum()/count() builders and different aliases, though its explanation of why strings come back is thorough and it adds the type-parser option; neither mentions .toQuery()/.toSQL() (B does show equivalent SQL).
